questions.q: In Shor's algorithm, what unitary does phase estimation get applied to, and what do its eigenvalues encode?
options: The classical gcd function, whose eigenvalues directly equal N's prime factors
The inverse QFT itself, applied to no particular unitary
The modular exponentiation map U_a: |x⟩ → |ax mod N⟩, whose eigenvalues are phases of the form e^(2πi·s/r), multiples of 1/r for the order r
The Hadamard gate, whose eigenvalues encode the number of qubits used
questions.explain: Shor's algorithm applies phase estimation to U_a, whose eigenvalues are multiples of 1/r, where r is the multiplicative order that period-finding is trying to recover.

questions.q: After phase estimation returns an estimate θ ≈ s/r in Shor's algorithm, what classical step recovers the actual integer r?
options: The continued-fractions algorithm
Repeating phase estimation with a different eigenvector
Classically diagonalizing U_a as a matrix
A second round of Hadamard gates
questions.explain: Continued fractions is the classical post-processing step that extracts the exact fraction s/r (and hence r) from phase estimation's decimal-like output.

questions.q: In quantum chemistry simulation, what does phase estimation applied to U = e^(iHt) recover?
options: The eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian H, which correspond to the system's allowed energy levels, including the ground-state energy
The exact number of atoms in the simulated molecule
A classical FFT of the molecule's structure
The period of a modular exponentiation sequence
questions.explain: Since U is the time-evolution operator for Hamiltonian H, phase estimation's output θ directly ties back to H's eigenvalues -- the system's energy levels.

questions.q: What role does phase estimation play inside the HHL algorithm for solving linear systems Ax = b?
options: It is used only to prepare the initial state |0⟩ on the counting register
It replaces the need for matrix A entirely
HHL does not use phase estimation at all; it uses only the QFT
It is used to extract (and allow manipulation/inversion of) the eigenvalues of matrix A, analogous to how it extracts eigenvalues of a Hamiltonian in chemistry simulation
questions.explain: HHL reduces to applying phase estimation to a unitary built from A, in order to access and invert A's eigenvalues as part of constructing the solution state.

questions.q: What is the general pattern connecting Shor's algorithm, quantum chemistry simulation, and HHL, as described in this lesson?
options: All three are purely classical algorithms with no quantum component

All three reuse the same phase estimation circuit (Hadamards, controlled-U^(2^k), inverse QFT, measure) on a problem-specific unitary, differing only in which U is chosen and what classical post-processing interprets the result
All three only work for factoring problems, not energy levels or linear systems
All three require building a completely different quantum circuit from scratch with no shared structure
questions.explain: The quantum circuit itself is unchanged across all three algorithms -- what varies is the specific unitary U and the classical interpretation of the resulting phase estimate.
